summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for acute worsening of left lower quadrant pain, similar to a recent hospitalization one week prior. She presented with nausea and functional impairment despite home medications. Initial labs showed hypokalemia, which resolved during the stay, and a stable normocytic anemia not deemed acute. A transvaginal ultrasound revealed normal pelvic anatomy with no new pathology. Pain was managed with continuation of home medications including gabapentin, tizanidine, tramadol, and lidocaine patch, without escalation to additional narcotics. The patient improved clinically, with resolution of abdominal tenderness and increased mobility. She was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her OB/GYN in two days for ongoing pain management and outpatient workup of anemia.
